title: Cross-functional roadmap sync prep - Sep 2024 (draft)
content:
Meeting: Cross-functional roadmap alignment sync (Product + Eng + Applied ML)
Date: 2024-09-09 10:00-11:00 PT (prep notes)
Owner / note-taker: Anika Rao
Attendees (ask to confirm): Jared (Product Lead), Priya (Eng Lead, serving runtime), Liam (Applied ML), Evan (solutions eng), + 1 SRE rep (TBD)
Purpose: quick alignment on Q4 roadmap priorities, validate capacity assumptions for new hosting features, confirm rollout gating criteria and ML evaluation plan. Keep to 45m decision-focused + 15m follow-ups.

Agenda (45m)
- 5m: Quick status & context (what changed since last sync)
- 15m: Priority decisions (pick order for the three hosting initiatives: Dedicated autoscale improvements, Private deployment onboarding flow, Optimize caching default changes)
- 10m: Capacity & risk review (GPU capacity, rollout windows, fallback behavior)
- 10m: ML evaluation / quality gating (applied ML: regen vs. baseline thresholds, eval prompt sets)
- 5m: Action items & owners, confirm next check-in cadence

Prep notes / background (TL;DR)
- Product proposal updated: prioritize Dedicated autoscale (improve tail latency and burst capacity) because a major customer is gating renewals on predictable burst behavior. See Confluence Roadmap Q4 (linked).
- Private deployment onboarding still higher effort (networking/KMS + install automation) and likely requires Dedicated engineering allocation of ~2 FTE for 6w to hit MVP.
- Optimize caching defaults: relatively low engineering effort, but risk to correctness if misconfigured for stateful chat. Need more applied-ML evals before default flip.

Key questions to bring to the meeting (decisions needed)
1) Do we reallocate 2 FTE from serving-runtime to Private deployment onboarding for a 6-week push (impacting other infra work)? (Decision owner: Priya)
2) Can we ship Dedicated autoscale MVP in a staged rollout (canary customers -> region-by-region) while keeping current SLA for hosted API? (Owner: Jared + Priya)
3) Are the current ML eval thresholds for caching safe to proceed with default ON for small sessions (<512 tokens)? Need applied-ML signoff. (Owner: Liam)

Notes to self / talking points
- Emphasize customer urgency on Dedicated (revenue risk). Have the customer quote ready (sales).
- For Private deployment ask: what are the minimum infra prerequisites? (network, KMS, image signing). Need SRE input.
- For caching: propose staged experiment: 10% traffic -> analyze regen rate / hallucination delta on core prompt set (RW-2123).

Capacity assumptions (to confirm in meeting)
- Serving-runtime: current spare capacity for Dedicated improvements ~1.5 FTE equivalent (optimizations + infra changes), but sustained 2 FTE needed to hit timeline.
- Applied ML: evaluation pipeline can run nightly evals; however manual annotation/edge-case triage needs ~0.25 FTE/2 weeks.
- Rollout windows: avoid major changes during Black Friday prep (Nov 15 - Dec 5) - set freeze for large infra rollouts.

Risks & mitigations
- Risk: Dedicated autoscale causes increased cost due to over-provisioning. Mitigation: implement conservative thresholds, add cost telemetry and per-customer caps.
- Risk: Caching default causes regression for long-conversation LLM outputs. Mitigation: session-length gating + early metric rollback path.
- Risk: Private deployment delays due to third-party KMS integration. Mitigation: deliver a basic flow that accepts customer-managed keys later in patch.

Concrete asks for attendees (prep items)
- Priya: come with an estimate on engineering effort (FTE-weeks) for Dedicated autoscale MVP and for Private onboarding (high-level breakdown). Also list dependencies on infra/SRE.
- Liam: bring current eval results for caching experiments (regen %, rouge/embedding drift) and a recommended threshold for safe default.
- Jared: provide the customer renewal timeline and priority ranking across Q4 features (so we can trade-off).
- Evan: impacts to solutions docs / install playbook for Private deployment - any blockers?

Draft decisions to propose (quick wins)
- Approve Dedicated autoscale as top priority for near-term roadmap, allocate 2 FTE for 6 weeks (propose start Sep 16).
- Do not flip caching default globally yet; run a staged 10% experiment for two weeks and re-evaluate.
- Defer full Private deployment onboarding until after autoscale MVP unless sales escalates (conditional).

Action items (post-meeting follow-up template)
- RW-A1: Priya to provide FTE-week breakdown for Dedicated autoscale + timeline by 2024-09-11. (owner: Priya Nanda, due: 2024-09-11)
- RW-A2: Liam to run 10% caching experiment, share initial metrics + obs in #product-roadmap + confluence page RW-2123 by 2024-09-18. (owner: Liam OConnor, due: 2024-09-18)
- RW-A3: Jared to confirm customer renewal date + gating criteria; provide sales contact for follow-up by 2024-09-10. (owner: Jared Kim, due: 2024-09-10)
- RW-A4: Evan to draft Private deployment install playbook outline and list missing artifacts (KMS, network diagrams) by 2024-09-13. (owner: Evan Brooks, due: 2024-09-13)
- RW-A5: Anika to update Confluence roadmap doc with agreed priorities + upload meeting notes and action items (owner: Anika Rao, due: 2024-09-10)

Possible follow-ups (if decisions change)
- If sales pushes Private deployment as non-negotiable, re-score priorities and propose a 3-way split (1.5 FTE Dedicated, 1.5 FTE Private) for Sep-Oct - need explicit approval from Eng director.
- If caching experiment shows >5% regen rate with >0.5% reconstruction failures, auto-rollback flags must be ready; schedule immediate post-mortem.

Misc (scratchpad)
- Jira tickets to reference: RW-2123 (caching eval), RW-2178 (dedicated autoscale epic), RW-2210 (private deployment onboarding).
- PRs: github.com/redwood-inference/rw-serving/pull/789 (autoscale prototype), github.com/redwood-inference/rw-optimize/pull/101 (caching infra)
- Confluence: Roadmap Q4 2024 (link above)

Notes style: keep this doc messy - will clean the final meeting notes and publish.

-- end of prep --
